column2: In the root, "Haum, homage to Shiva"; "Om Ham Hum Him Haum" to the head; "Hrim" to the crest; "Haim" armor; "Ha" the missile; and to him with his retinue.
One should give Shiva foot-water, rinsing water and arghya; scent, flowers, incense, lamp, food-offering and rinsing water;
hand-rubbing, betel, mouth-perfume and a mirror; having placed on the god's head durva, rice and the sacred thread,
having repeated the root-mantra a hundred and eight times, consecrated with the heart-mantra; a sword wrapped in leather, protected with kusha and flowers,
joined with rice and the mudra, to Shiva with the name Udbhava: "Accept the repetition done by us for the secrecy of the most secret.
May accomplishment be mine, by your grace, when you are established in me." Having recited the first verse, the enjoyer, with the right hand to Shambhu,
with the root-atom and arghya-water one should offer on the boon-hand: "Whatever good or evil we do, god, always,
cast that of mine, standing at Shiva's feet — Hum Ksha — O Shankara. Shiva is giver, Shiva is enjoyer, Shiva is all this world.
Shiva conquers everywhere; he who is Shiva, that I am." Having recited these two verses, one should offer the repetition to the god.

Having given a tenth part for the limbs of Shiva, one should offer arghya and praise. Having circumambulated, one should bow with the eightfold prostration to the Eight-formed; having bowed one should worship in a picture, in fire and elsewhere by meditation and the rest.
Burnt by the missile-mantra, one should again throw the darbha into the fire; having thrown into ghee the kusha tied in a knot, of a span's measure,
one should imagine two sides, Ida and the others, three in the ghee; having taken ghee in the ladle by three portions in order, one should offer.

In the fire "sva," in the ghee "ha," one should throw the rest of the ghee in order. "Om Ham, to Agni, svaha. Om Ham, to Soma, svaha. Om Ham, to Agni-Soma, svaha," for opening the eyes, in the fire's three eyes, in the face.
With a ladle full of ghee one should offer the fourth oblation: "Om Ham, to Agni Svishtakrit, svaha." Having consecrated with the six limbs, one should awaken with the cow-mudra.
Having covered with armor, one should guard the ghee with the arrow-atom; with a drop of ghee from the heart, having sprinkled, one should purify.

The union of the face-oblations and making the faces one: "Om Ham, to Sadyojata, svaha; Om Ham, to Vamadeva, svaha; Om Ham, to Aghora, svaha; Om, to Tatpurusha, svaha; Om Ham, to Ishana, svaha" — with each ghee oblation one should do the face-pouring.

Om Ham, to Sadyojata and Vamadeva, svaha. Om Ham, to Vamadeva and Aghora, svaha. Om Ham, to Aghora and Tatpurusha, svaha. Om Ham, to Tatpurusha and Ishana, svaha — thus with these mantras one should do the connection of faces in order, going from Agni toward Vayu, from Nirriti to Shiva,

one should make the faces one with a stream of ghee from the ladle: "Om Ham, to Sadyojata, Vamadeva, Aghora, Tatpurusha and Ishana, svaha." Thus in the chosen face the inclusion of the faces has that form.
Having worshipped the fire with Ishana, having given three oblations with the weapon-mantra, one should do it with the name of the Self of all: "You are the Shiva-fire, Hutashana."
In the fire dismissed, the two worshipped by the heart, the fulfilling of rule — with the root-mantra ending in vaushat one should give the full oblation according to rule.
Then in the lotus of the heart one should worship, with limbs and army, the radiant supreme as before; having invoked, requested permission, one should satisfy Shiva.
Having made the joining of the channels of the sacrificial fire and Shiva by oneself, one should do the oblation with the power and root-atom, with the limbs a tenth.
Oblation of ghee a karsha, likewise of milk and honey; of curds a power-measure oblation; of pudding a handful.
As appropriate of all food a fistful; of parched grain a handful; of roots three pieces by their own measure.
Of cooked food half a mouthful; one should offer five subtle ones. Of sugarcane the measure of a joint; of creepers two fingers;
flower and leaf by own measure; of fuel sticks ten fingers; moon, sandal, saffron, musk, Yaksha-mud;
of the measure of a pea; guggulu like a jujube stone; one should offer an eighth part of tubers by rule, the highest.
Thus one should complete the oblation, then with the Brahma-seed words; having placed a ladle full of ghee, the Sruva face down,
having placed a flower on the tip of the ladle, then with the left hand, again holding both with the right, in a conch-like mudra,
risen up, half-bodied, with feet together, standing with fuel, placing its root at the navel, with eyes fixed on the ladle's tip,
having gone out by abandoning the cause beginning with Brahma, through the Sushumna, bringing it to the end of the left breast, unwearied, the root of those two,
one should utter the root-mantra indistinctly ending in vaushat. One should offer ghee in that fire in a barley-thin stream.
Having given rinsing water, sandal, betel and the rest, having devotedly saluted its ashes, one should make supreme obeisance.
Then having worshipped the fire, with the missile-mantra ending in phat withdrawing the coverings by the mudra of withdrawal and saying "Forgive,"
those radiant enclosures, by inhalation with the heart-atom, with supreme faith one should establish in one's own heart-lotus.
Having taken the first of all the cooked food and made two circles, one should give offerings inside and outside in the southeast near the pit:
Om Ham, to the Rudras, svaha in the east; to the Mothers in the south likewise; in the west "Ham, to the Ganas, svaha; this offering is for them."
In the north "Ham" to the Yakshas; in the northeast "Ham" to the planets; in the fire direction "Ham" to the Asuras; to the Rakshasas an offering in the southwest.
In the northwest "Ham" to the Nagas; in the middle to the stars; "Ham, to the zodiac signs, svaha" in the fire; to the Vishvedevas in the southwest likewise;
in the west to the field-guardian — the inner offering is declared. In the second circle, outside, to Indra, Agni and Yama,
to Nirriti, to the lord of waters, to Vayu, to the guardian of wealth, to Ishana in the east and others; in Ishana, "homage to Brahma";
in the southwest "to Vishnu, svaha"; outside, the offering for crows and the rest. The mantras contained in the two offerings, by the mudra of withdrawal, in oneself.
In a crescent or chisel-shaped form one should worship the four-faced; one should repeat as able, a tenth of it for the limbs.
Cows, land, gold, clothes and the like, jewels, gold and ornaments — leaving aside the rest, the remnant should be offered to Chandesha.
Things to lick and chew and the rest, betel, garland and ointment, remnant and food — "I have given to you by Shiva's command.
All this ritual section, Chanda, I have done at your command, more or less through delusion; may it be always complete for me."
Having thus informed the lord of the gods, having given arghya, remembering him, with the mantra of the Destroyer's form slowly with the mudra of withdrawal,

with the root-mantra joined with inhalation one should unite the mantras in the self. The place where the remnant was removed should be plastered with cow-dung and water; having sprinkled, dismissed the arghya and the rest, having rinsed, one should do another.
Homage to the Sun, to Brihaspati, to the lord of creatures; to all the gods, and to all the Vishvedevas.
Ham, to Agni Svishtakrit — one should worship these in the east and others; having given an oblation ending in svaha, having asked forgiveness, one should dismiss.
At the hearth, in the right arm, one should worship "homage to Dharma"; in the left arm "to Adharma"; in the vessel of sour gruel and the like,
to the one turning through taste, to Varuna, to water-fire; Vighnaraja at the house door; in the grinding stone "homage to Subhaga";
Om, homage to Raudrika; homage to Girika in the mortar one should worship; "homage to you, dear to strength, the weapon," in the pestle one should worship;
in the broom "the deity said"; to Kama in the bed; to Skanda in the middle pillar; having given the house-offering,
then one should eat in a golden vessel or on lotus leaves and the like. The teacher, the seeker, the son, the one observing silence,
should avoid banyan, ashvattha, arka, vata, visarja and bhallataka. Having taken water first with the breaths and the rest joined with Om,
having given five oblations ending in svaha and kindled the belly-fire: Naga, Kurma, Krikara, Devadatta, Dhananjaya —
to these sub-winds, svaha, with water of the ashana; having offered food and the rest, the man should drink the remaining water.
You are the spreading-cover of immortality; then one should give the breath-oblations: "To prana, svaha; to apana; to samana" likewise,
to udana and vyana; having eaten one should rinse. "You are the covering of immortality": in the body the winds of food and the rest.
In the directions the guardians beginning with Indra, Vishnu, Brahma, Shiva and the rest. Having properly taken the Vardhani following the back of the pot,
the mantra-master should have Shiva's command heard, facing from the east to Ishana; with an unbroken stream of water he should utter the root-mantra,
one should turn it all around, in the form of a weapon, for protection. Having first placed the pot, for the weapon on its left,
in the pot with a full seat, in a steady seat, one should worship the god; in the Vardhani, standing in Om, the weapon then among the two,
one should make the union of yoni and linga with the linga mudra. Having offered in the pot the sword of awareness and repeating the root-mantra,
with a tenth of that one should declare protection in the Vardhani. Having worshipped Ganesha in the northwest and Hara with the five nectars and the rest,
one should bathe as before, having worshipped; in the pit the Shiva-fire; having duly made the porridge purified by the Sampata oblation,
by the distinction of the god-first and self, one should divide it in three with the ladle; having given two portions to Shiva and Agni, one should keep a portion for oneself.
With an arrow and hide the tooth-cleaner should be given first; from that, or with the Ghora and Shikha mantras, in the south and west earth;
with Sadyojata and the heart in the north, made small; water with the left head; in Ishana water with scent;
the five cow-products and palasha leaf-cups on all sides; in the northeast one should give flowers, in the fire direction rochana,
agaru in the southwest; in the northwest the four-equal; all the oblation materials with Sadyojata kusha;
staff, rosary-thread, loincloth and begging bowl for the embodied one; collyrium, saffron, oil, a probe, a hair-cleanser;
betel and mirror should be given; in the north rochana also; seat, sandals, bowl, yoga-cloth, umbrella
in the northeast with Ishana's mantra one should give for Ishana's satisfaction. In the east the porridge with ghee, and scent and the rest in a new vessel.
Having taken the earlier purifiers, sprinkled with arghya-water, purified by Samhita mantras, bringing them near the fire,
having covered with a black antelope skin and the like, remembering Shiva made of the year — the witness of all actions, the protector, the imperishable —
by application of "sva" and "ha," again with the mantra collection, one should purify the threads twenty-one times.
One should wrap the house and the rest with threads; one should give scent and the rest to the Sun. Having rinsed before the worshipped, with placement and arghya made,
to Nandi and others, then the one called scent and the house-deity, having entered, to weapons and guardians of the world by their own names in Shiva's pot.
